newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Aug 15.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 41 percent decline in its turnover, dragging the BSE short-term debentures index down 44.57 points in the week to August 15.
Total turnover fell to 59.995 million dinars ($9.85 million) from 101.9 million dinars a week ago, while the number of deals rose to 137 from 102.
The BSE index fell 20.76 percent to 170.16 points. It stood at 214.73 index points a week ago.

While some analysts saw market activity falling prey to a late summer lull, traders said the decline followed the central bank raising the reserve requirement for commercial banks to 20 from 15 percent.
But both traders and analysts agreed the declining activity would not last long.
"Whenever things get worse for banks, issuing companies turn to the market for funds," an analyst told Reuters.

Traders insisted banks, with their liquidity swelling over the past two months after Serbia sold part of its Telecom for close to $1 billion and converted part of the receipts into dinars, have been stealing the bourse clients away by attracting them with higher interest on bank deposits.
Banks have been offering 8.00 percent monthly interest on their deposits and treasury bills at times when average rates on the market stood between a monthly 5.00 and 6.00 percent.
The latest increase in the reserve requirement is expected to mop up some surplus liquidity from the banking sector and redirect borrowers to the market, traders said.
For the week ending August 15, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 120 deals totalling 29.064 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded 11 times for a total of 1.661 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between 5.00 and 8.00 percent per month, while maturity stood between 10 and 180 days.
* The bourse reported three deals in the state T-bills totalling 21 million dinars.
* The central bank short-term bonds traded once for a volume of 8 million dinars.

* The BSE issued no details on the over-the-counter trade. NOTE -- The BSE short-term debentures index is calculated on volume, interest rate and maturity of the most frequently bourse-traded commercial paper and treasury bills. Index base is 1996. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
